original_record.subject: accounts
original_record.question: When a transaction causes an asset account to increase, there is

options.A: a decrease of equal amount in the owner’s equity account
options.B: an increase in a liability account
options.C: an increase of equal amount in another asset account
options.D: a decrease of equal amount in a liability account.

original_record.ai_explanation: When an asset increases, the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) requires a corresponding increase in either liabilities or equity; this could be an increase in a liability.

records.hold_reason: An asset increase can be financed by a liability, equity or another asset decrease. The source asks for an unconditional consequence, so its proposed liability increase is not uniquely necessary.

original_record.subject: accounts
original_record.question: If the inventory at the end of the current year is understated and the error is not caught during the following year, the effect is to

options.A: understate income this year and understate in next year
options.B: overstate income this year and overstate in next year
options.C: understate this year’s income with no effect on next year’s
options.D: overstate the income for the two-year period.

original_record.ai_explanation: Understated ending inventory in year 1 overstates COGS and understates year 1 income; it becomes understated opening inventory in year 2, understating COGS and overstating year 2 income, but the error reverses—however, the net effect across both years shows understatement in year 1 and understatement in year 2 due to the timing of the correction.

records.hold_reason: An understated closing stock reduces this year’s profit and overstates next year’s profit if next closing stock is correct. None of the printed alternatives states that combination.
